newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's Ershad takes back expelled leader.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's Ershad takes back expelled leader.

text.p: Bangladesh's former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad on Thursday recalled ex-prime minister Kazi Zafar Ahmed to his Jatiya party, two days after expelling him for "overstepping party lines".
"The party chairman (Ershad) has withdrawn the expulsion order," a party press release said. It did not say what prompted Ershad's move.
Ahmed declined to comment on the reversal.
Ershad fired Ahmed on Tuesday after he was involved in a brawl with other party leaders at a Jatiya rally in Dhaka.

"Kazi Zafar Ahmed has been expelled from the party for speaking against the party's policy and ideals, and against the interest of the party chairman (Ershad)," a Jatiya Party statement said on Tuesday night.
Jatiya sources on Tuesday said Ahmed had defied earlier requests by Ershad not to make offending comments about government policy but to stress the Jatiya Party's own independent stance.
Ershad seized power in 1982 and became president after 1984 elections. He was toppled in December 1990 and then jailed soon after on corruption charges. He was freed last January.
Jatiya has 33 seats in the 330 member parliament.
